errors.description: There is no topstitch anywhere along the pocket mouth. I rectified the pocket-mouth edge (line fit x = -0.36034*y + 422.11, 305 inliers, rms 0.53 px, y 395-700) and averaged 650 perpendicular cross-sections. The mean profile contains exactly one feature: a shadow trough at t = -1.0 px (grey 52.2) and a specular ridge at t = +2.0 px (grey 99.9) — the signature of a bare pressed fold — then monotonic shading fall-off. In the 6-12 px band where a 0.15 cm stitch must sit (see px/cm below), the largest deviation from that fall-off is ~0.7 grey levels against a local texture sigma of ~21 grey levels (SNR 0.03). A periodicity test confirms it: high-passed along-line FFT at every offset from -40 to +40 px gives a dominant period of 4.1-4.5 px at EVERY offset — that is the weave, equally strong 40 px out in open cloth — and power in the stitch-pitch band (10-24 px = 1.7-4.0 mm) peaks at t = +34.5 px, out in plain cloth, i.e. noise. Direct 8x inspection at y = 430, 560 and 680 shows a rolled edge with zero thread and zero needle penetrations. The same test on candidate-1 also finds no stitch, so this was never rendered, not lost.
errors.expected: a single machine topstitch row running the full pocket mouth, set 0.15 cm (approx. 8-10 px at this frame's scale) in from the folded edge, with resolvable individual needle penetrations at roughly 2-3 mm pitch — the one feature the option exists to sell
errors.actual: a bare pressed pocket-mouth fold with no stitching of any kind; the discriminating feature is entirely absent
errors.correction: Regenerate with the stitch as the literal subject: an unbroken machine topstitch row parallel to the pocket-mouth fold, offset 0.15 cm, individual stitches visible, thread matched to the cloth. State the stitch pitch explicitly in the prompt (2.5 mm) so the model has a countable target rather than an adjective.

notes:
VERDICT: FAIL — do not publish. Two critical findings.

FAULT-FIXED ANSWER, MEASURED. The fault was framing, with the operative test "a macro close-up where the stitch is plainly resolvable." Landmark: waistband depth (top edge to waistband bottom seam), validated by overlay in both frames. candidate-1 = 146 px (y30-y176), candidate-2 = 242 px (y105-y347), identical 880x1168 frames. Magnification rose 1.66x. Scale: the drawing carries NO printed dimension callout, so no centimetre figure is strictly recoverable from it — every cm below is derived from the tailoring convention that a bespoke trouser waistband is 3.5-4.5 cm deep, and is given as a range. On that basis candidate-2 is 54-69 px/cm, so 0.15 cm subtends 8-10 px. Independent cross-check: belt-loop outer width 75 px (x 605-680); a suit-trouser loop is 1.0-1.2 cm, giving 62-75 px/cm — consistent, and an upper bound since the loop is foreshortened on the curved waistband. So the geometric half of the fault improved: 0.15 cm went from ~5.5 px to ~9 px and is now resolvable in principle. But faultFixed = false, on two grounds: (a) the frame is still a hip shot, not a macro — the subject sits in the left third with ~10.5 cm of dead cloth on the right, against a correction that asked for "only a few centimetres of cloth either side"; and (b) the stitch is not plainly resolvable because there is no stitch. A frame cannot pass a "the stitch must be legible" test when the stitch was never rendered.

CORRECTING THE PRIOR QC. Attempt 1's finding said the stitch "spans roughly a pixel." Measured, candidate-1 was ~36.5 px/cm, so 0.15 cm spanned ~5.5 px there — the prior QC was wrong by about 5x, and it diagnosed a framing problem when the actual defect was a missing feature. That misdiagnosis is why attempt 2 burned credits on a crop change and shipped the same defect. The next correction must lead with the missing stitch, not the crop.

WHAT I COULD NOT MEASURE. (1) No absolute centimetre scale is recoverable — the drawing has no dimension callout; all cm figures are ranges from an assumed waistband depth and are labelled as such. (2) Left/right symmetry is not assessable: the drawing marks both pockets (left 5777 px, right 5837 px, slopes 15.64 and 15.60 deg, symmetric to 0.04 deg) but only one hip is in frame — symmetry scored 75 to reflect "unverified", not "passed". (3) The drawn run length (5.54x waistband depth) cannot be checked because the mouth exits frame. (4) Stitch pitch, thread weight and thread colour are unmeasurable because no stitch exists.

METHOD NOTES. The stitch-absence finding rests on three independent checks that agree: the averaged perpendicular profile (one fold signature, nothing else, SNR 0.03 in the 6-12 px band), the along-line FFT sweep (dominant period 4.1-4.5 px at every one of 321 offsets = the weave, stitch-band power peaking at t=+34.5 px out in open cloth = noise), and direct 8x visual inspection at three points. I checked the extracted line's span rather than trusting the first fit: the initial tracker returned only 273/600 inliers, so I refit on clean segments — y395-700 gave n=305 at rms 0.53 px, and the lower segment independently agreed (19.68 vs 19.82 deg), so the angle finding is not an artefact of a partial run. I also verified I was measuring the pocket mouth and not the pleat or the side seam by overlaying the fit on the image before taking any number from it.

NO WRITES were made to data-store/ or public/images/generated/. Working files are in the session scratchpad only; nothing in .craft-pipeline was modified.
